subject: Action checklist: transient request queuing in US-West (customer impact)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lithiumai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Action checklist: transient request queuing in US-West (customer impact)

Hi Alex / Lithium ops team,

Quick note to let you know we detected a short-lived increase in request queuing impacting p95 latency for hosted inference in the US-West region starting ~09:00 PDT. You may see elevated p95s and some increased retry behavior until our mitigation completes.

What we have done so far (completed):
- Enabled reserved-pool routing for your account to move traffic off the best-effort queue.
- Enabled burst capacity for the pool servicing your region.
- Applied aggressive prefix cache reuse on active conversational sessions to reduce token work.

Immediate ask from you:
- Can you confirm whether your integrations saw any 5xx responses or significant client retries between 08:50–09:10 PDT? A quick note back is fine.

Planned next actions (30–60m):
- Engineering to finish a background cache warmup for the affected model families.
- If latency does not improve within 45 minutes, we will initiate a failover route to our secondary US cluster (we will coordinate so keys/regions remain consistent).

Attachment: runbook_snapshot.pdf (excerpt of the on-call checklist we used).

We’ll update you as mitigation progresses; short-term goal is to restore p95 to baseline. Postmortem & root cause will follow.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lithiumai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@lithiumai.com
Date: Wed, 4 Oct 2028 09:18:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Action checklist: transient request queuing in US-West (customer impact)

Thanks Neha — we saw elevated response times and about ~0.4% 502s across a small percentage of requests around 08:55–09:05 PDT.

Quick details from our side:
- Error rate spike corresponded to our highest-traffic indexer job (runs hourly)
- We have logs (attached snippet in our internal system) showing retries during that window

Is there an ETA on the cache warmup or the failover? Our ops team is watching dashboards and will throttle that indexer if you suggest.

On Wed, Oct 4, 2028 at 9:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick note to let you know we detected a short-lived increase in request queuing impacting p95 latency for hosted inference in the US-West region starting ~09:00 PDT.

Appreciate the quick reply — thumbs-up on the throttle for the indexer if needed. Any timeline helps so we can coordinate.

—Alex
Alex Turner

alex.turner@lithiumai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Oct 2028 09:30:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Action checklist: transient request queuing in US-West (customer impact)

Neha / Ben — ops update:

Status now:
- Reserved-pool routing confirmed for LithiumAI (traffic shifted at 09:14 PDT).
- p95 for the affected model family reduced from ~1.6s -> ~0.45s over the following 12 minutes.
- No further 502 waves observed after 09:22 PDT.

Engineering actions in progress:
- Background KV cache warmup running (expected completion ~09:55 PDT).
- Investigating whether a degraded kernel selection path was triggered for a subset of hosts; creating an ops ticket (HS-234582).

Customer notes: Alex reported 0.4% 502s during the spike — they have paused their indexer temporarily.

Suggested next steps (owner):
- Neha: communicate ETA & ask Lithium if they want scheduled downtime windows for heavier jobs (ACTION: send follow-up).
- Ben: please open a post-incident thread with infra and attach logs from hosts usw-rt-12/13 (ACTION: create).
- Infra-oncall: preserve request/trace samples from 08:45–09:30 (ACTION: retain).

I’m adding the runbook excerpt to the incident record and attaching the interim mitigation_playbook.md.

Marissa Cole
Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lithiumai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Bcc: legal@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Oct 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Mitigation complete & next steps — US-West transient queuing (follow-up)

Alex / Lithium team,

Thanks again for the quick coordination yesterday. Brief summary and next steps:

What happened (short):
- A transient request queuing condition in the US-West serving layer caused elevated p95 and a small spike in 5xx errors for a narrow window (~08:50–09:10 PDT).

What we did:
- Shifted LithiumAI traffic to reserved pool; enabled burst capacity and ran KV cache warmup.
- Observed p95 return to baseline within ~20 minutes of the first mitigation actions.

Current state:
- No active impact detected in your account or the broader US-West cluster as of 15:30 PDT today.
- We have preserved traces and collected host logs; Ben will attach the log slices to the incident HS-234582.

Action items / ask from LithiumAI:
- If you plan recurring heavy indexer runs, reply with a suggested schedule window so we can coordinate capacity ahead of time.
- If you want us to open a formal support ticket for deeper log correlation, say the word and we’ll do it.

Postmortem & timing:
- We will publish a succinct post-incident note on our status page (link below) and follow with a more detailed RCA within 5 business days after root cause analysis.

Status and artifacts:
- Incident record: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/USW-2028-10-04-queueing
- Internal ops doc (interim mitigation): mitigation_playbook.md
- Runbook excerpt: runbook_snapshot.pdf
- HubSpot: HS-234582

If anything changes or you see residual issues, please reply directly to me and I’ll escalate.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
